input.quote: Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Sections 13.1–13.3 meet the preferred position (Affiliates and contractors named, perpetual and irrevocable paid-up licence, revocation only for uncured material breach, transfer to Affiliate or successor). Section 14.2, however, grants a Deliverable licence that is revocable at will, non-transferable, limited to the Order Form term, and silent on Affiliates and contractors — a walk-away term that conflicts with 13.2 and 14.3. The redline conforms 14.2 to the Section 13 grant with the smallest edit.

proposal.summary: Conform the Deliverable licence in 14.2 to the perpetual, irrevocable grant in 13.2, covering Affiliates and contractors and transferable to successors.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have conformed the Deliverable licence to the perpetual, irrevocable grant already agreed in Sections 13.2 and 13.3, so it covers our Affiliates and contractors and is transferable to a successor. A licence that is revocable at will and expires with the Order Form term would leave us unable to keep using work product we have paid for.

ops.oldText: Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
ops.newText: Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf receive a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, reproduce, display, modify, and create derivative works from each Deliverable for Customer's business, transferable to an Affiliate or successor in accordance with Section 13.3 and revocable or suspendable only as permitted by Section 13.3.
